title: Chicken Karahi
description: A bold, dhaba-style Chicken Karahi made with large 2-inch cubes of Costco boneless chicken thighs seared on high flame, enriched with Better Than Bouillon chicken paste, a generous cube of butter, and heavy cream, and finished with garam/kari masala, kasoori methi, fresh curry leaves, almond-cut green chillies, and lemon.
note: SALT & CREAM NOTE: Better Than Bouillon Chicken Base paste is already quite salty — taste the gravy before adding extra salt. Cutting the Costco boneless chicken thighs into generous 2-inch cubes keeps them juicy during high-flame karahi cooking. Drop the flame to medium-low before stirring in the 3 tbsp heavy cream so it emulsifies smoothly without splitting.

referenceVideo.title: Chef Ajay Kumar — Chicken Karahi (YouTube Short)

modifications: Used 2 bags (~1 kg) of Costco boneless chicken thighs cut into large ~2-inch cubes instead of small bone-in chicken pieces.
Used 2 big tomatoes instead of 5 smaller tomatoes.
Added 1.5 tbsp Better Than Bouillon chicken base paste for deeper savory flavor.
Added a 2-3 inch cube of butter right before covering and cooking for 4-5 minutes.
Stirred in 3 tbsp heavy whipping cream after the 4-5 minute covered butter cook.
2 minutes before turning off the flame, added 1 tbsp garam masala (or kari masala) along with kasoori methi, fresh curry leaves, and almond-cut (diagonally sliced) green chillies.

sections.name: Fresh Karahi Spice Mix (Dry Roast & Coarsely Grind)

items.text: Costco Boneless Chicken Thighs (Cut into large ~2-inch cubes)
Better Than Bouillon Chicken Base Paste
Freshly Ground Karahi Masala (From spice mix above)
Warm Water (As needed to adjust consistency)
Salt (Adjust carefully — bouillon paste already contains salt)
Butter (2-3 inch cube, added before covering)
Garam Masala or Kari Masala (2 mins before flame off)
Toasted Kasoori Methi (Dried Fenugreek Leaves, crushed)

steps.title: Step A: Dry Roast & Grind Karahi Masala
instructions: Dry roast 2 tbsp coriander seeds, 2 tbsp cumin seeds, 1 tbsp black peppercorns, and 4 dried red chillies in a dry pan over low flame for 2-3 minutes until aromatic and slightly brown (do not burn).
Let cool briefly, then grind or pound to a coarse, rustic Karahi Masala consistency. Set aside.

steps.title: Step B: High-Flame Chicken Sear
instructions: Heat 100 ml cooking oil in a wide karahi or heavy-bottomed wok over high flame.

Add the 2 bags of Costco boneless chicken thighs cut into large ~2-inch cubes. Sear on high flame for 4-5 minutes, tossing occasionally until the chicken takes on good golden color and reaches about 50% doneness.
Carefully spoon out and remove any excess oil from the pan before building the base.

steps.title: Step C: Tomato Base, Bouillon & Spices
instructions: Add 3 tbsp ginger-garlic paste and stir well on medium-high flame until the raw aroma disappears.
Add the 2 big halved/chopped tomatoes and a splash of warm water. Cover and cook for 7-8 minutes until the tomatoes turn completely pulpy and skins loosen.
Remove the loosened tomato skins with tongs and mash the tomatoes thoroughly into the sauce using the back of a fork.

Keep the flame on medium. Add 1.5 tbsp Better Than Bouillon chicken paste, 1 tsp turmeric powder, 2 tbsp Kashmiri red chilli powder, 1 tbsp black pepper powder, 2 tbsp freshly ground Karahi masala, and salt to taste (taste first since the bouillon paste is salty).
Stir thoroughly and cook the dry spices for 1-2 minutes until fragrant and deeply colored.

steps.title: Step D: Butter-Covered Cook & Heavy Cream
instructions: Before covering the pan, add the 2-3 inch cube of butter directly into the karahi.
Cover tightly and cook on medium flame for 4-5 minutes until the butter melts into a rich, silky gravy and the large 2-inch chicken cubes are cooked through and tender.
Uncover, lower the flame to medium-low, and stir in 3 tbsp heavy whipping cream until smoothly emulsified into the sauce.

dumInstruction: About 2 minutes before turning off the flame, add 1 tbsp garam masala (or kari masala), 1 tbsp crushed toasted kasoori methi, 2 sprigs fresh curry leaves, and the almond-cut (diagonally sliced) green chillies. Give a gentle stir and simmer for 2 minutes so the aromatics infuse into the creamy karahi sauce. Turn off the heat, garnish with 2 tbsp chopped fresh coriander leaves and sliced ginger juliennes, and squeeze half a lemon over the top to brighten the dish and balance the richness. Serve hot straight from the karahi with naan, roti, or steamed rice.
